questions.question: Newton's first law of motion (law of inertia) states that:

options.B: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
options.C: A body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an external force
options.D: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction

questions.explanation: Inertia is the resistance to change in motion; it is proportional to mass.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: According to Newton's second law, force equals:
questions.explanation: F = m × a; the unit of force is the newton (kg·m/s²).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The ground reaction force during walking is an example of Newton's:
questions.explanation: When the foot pushes on the ground, the ground pushes back with an equal and opposite force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Vectors have magnitude and direction (force, velocity, acceleration, displacement); scalars have magnitude only (mass, speed, distance, time).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Torque (moment of force) is calculated as:

options.C: Force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation

questions.explanation: Torque = F × moment arm; it is maximal when the force is applied perpendicular to the lever at the greatest distance.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Work done by a muscle is equal to:

options.B: Force multiplied by the distance moved in the direction of the force

questions.explanation: Work = F × d (joule); power = work/time (watt).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The unit of power is the:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In the standing human body in anatomical position, the centre of gravity lies approximately:

options.A: Anterior to the second sacral vertebra

questions.explanation: Approximately 55% of standing height (just anterior to S2); it changes with posture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Stability of a body is increased by:

options.C: Moving the line of gravity to the edge of the base
options.D: Widening the base of support and lowering the centre of gravity

questions.explanation: A wide base and low centre of mass require a greater force to tip the body.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The force of friction between two surfaces is proportional to:

options.C: The normal (perpendicular) force pressing them together and the coefficient of friction

questions.explanation: F = μN; it opposes sliding and is relevant to gait and walking aids.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A body is in static equilibrium when:

options.B: It is moving at high speed
options.C: The sum of all forces and the sum of all torques acting on it equals zero
options.D: Only the forces sum to zero

questions.explanation: Both translational and rotational equilibrium conditions must be met.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In a first-class lever the:

options.A: Axis is always at the end
options.B: Resistance lies between the axis and effort
options.C: Effort lies between the axis and resistance
options.D: Axis lies between the effort and the resistance

questions.explanation: Example: neck extension by posterior neck muscles (head on atlanto-occipital joint); a see-saw.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A second-class lever has:

options.A: The resistance between the axis and the effort
options.B: The effort between the axis and resistance
options.C: The axis between effort and resistance

questions.explanation: Example: plantar flexion rising on the toes; it favours force (mechanical advantage greater than 1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Most levers in the human body are:

options.C: Third-class, in which the effort lies between the axis and the resistance

questions.explanation: Example: biceps brachii flexing the elbow. They favour speed and range of motion over force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Mechanical advantage of a lever is the ratio of the:

options.A: Effort arm to the resistance arm
options.D: Resistance arm to the effort arm only

questions.explanation: MA = effort arm / resistance arm. MA > 1 means less effort is needed to move the load.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Flexion of the elbow by the biceps with a weight in the hand is an example of a:
questions.explanation: The muscle effort acts between the axis (elbow) and the resistance (weight in the hand).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a second-class lever in the body?

options.C: Elevating the arm with the deltoid

questions.explanation: Calf muscle effort is at the heel (calcaneus) with the resistance (body weight through the tibia) lying between the axis (toes) and the effort.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The hip joint is a:
questions.explanation: Triaxial; movements: flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The first carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is a:
questions.explanation: Allows flexion/extension, abduction/adduction and opposition.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The atlantoaxial (median) joint is a:
questions.explanation: Rotation of the atlas about the dens of the axis gives 50% of cervical rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The number of degrees of freedom of a hinge joint such as the elbow (humeroulnar) is:
questions.explanation: Uniaxial joints have 1 degree of freedom; condyloid 2; ball-and-socket 3.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The close-packed position of the hip joint is:

options.B: Full extension with medial rotation and abduction

questions.explanation: Close-packed: ligaments taut and surfaces maximally congruent; the loose-packed position is 30° flexion, 30° abduction and slight lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The scapulohumeral rhythm during arm elevation is approximately:

options.A: 2° of glenohumeral motion for every 1° of scapulothoracic motion

questions.explanation: Of 180° elevation, about 120° occurs at the glenohumeral joint and 60° at the scapulothoracic joint (2:1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: During full elevation of the arm the clavicle:

options.D: Rotates posteriorly about its long axis by about 30–50°

questions.explanation: Posterior rotation of the clavicle allows the scapula to upwardly rotate and permits complete elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The normal carrying angle of the elbow in adults is about:
questions.explanation: It is formed by the long axes of the arm and forearm in the anatomical position; valgus > 15° is cubitus valgus.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The ‘screw-home’ mechanism of the knee refers to:

options.A: Automatic lateral rotation of the tibia on the femur during the last 20° of extension
options.C: Medial rotation of the femur in flexion

questions.explanation: Locking of the knee in extension; the popliteus unlocks it by medially rotating the tibia on the femur (or laterally rotating the femur).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The Q-angle of the knee is formed by:

options.B: A line from the ASIS to the centre of the patella and a line from the patella to the tibial tubercle

questions.explanation: Normal Q-angle is about 13° in men and 18° in women; larger values predispose to patellar maltracking.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which is NOT a function of the patella?

options.B: Increasing the lever arm of the quadriceps

questions.explanation: The patella increases the moment arm of the quadriceps, concentrates force, and protects the joint; it does not affect stride length.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Excessive femoral anteversion is associated with:
questions.explanation: The normal anteversion angle in adults is about 15°; excess causes in-toeing, patellar squint and increased hip medial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The normal neck-shaft angle of the femur in the adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Coxa vara <120°; coxa valga >135°.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which structure is the primary static support of the medial longitudinal arch?

options.A: Plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament and plantar aponeurosis

questions.explanation: Tibialis posterior is the main dynamic support; the arch is also supported by the long plantar ligament and the windlass mechanism of the plantar fascia.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A muscle can generate its maximum active tension when it is at:
questions.explanation: Optimal overlap of actin and myosin filaments occurs near resting length (Blix curve).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In concentric contraction, as the velocity of shortening increases, the force the muscle can produce:
questions.explanation: Hill's curve: force falls as shortening velocity rises; eccentric force increases with the speed of lengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Compared with parallel muscle fibres, pennate muscles of the same volume have:

options.C: A larger physiological cross-sectional area, producing greater force but less excursion

questions.explanation: Pennation packs more fibres per unit volume; examples: gastrocnemius, deltoid, rectus femoris.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Active insufficiency occurs when:

options.B: A multi-joint muscle is shortened over all its joints and cannot generate effective force
options.C: A muscle is stretched over two joints

questions.explanation: Example: making a tight fist with the wrist fully flexed is weaker because finger flexors are shortened.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The tenodesis action in the hand means that:

options.B: Wrist flexion causes active finger extension
options.C: Wrist extension causes passive finger flexion by tension in the finger flexor tendons

questions.explanation: Used functionally in C6 tetraplegia; finger flexor tendon shortening should therefore not be stretched.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The muscle that is mainly responsible for a movement is called the:
questions.explanation: Antagonists oppose the movement; fixators stabilise a joint; synergists assist.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The primary hip abductors are the:

options.C: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Innervated by the superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The main action of gluteus maximus is:
questions.explanation: Powerful during stair climbing and rising from a chair; inferior gluteal nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which component of the quadriceps also acts as a hip flexor?
questions.explanation: It is the only biarticular head, crossing the hip and knee.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The primary function of the vastus medialis obliquus (VMO) is:

options.A: To stabilise the patella medially and resist lateral subluxation

questions.explanation: Its oblique fibres counteract the lateral pull of the quadriceps and ITB.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The hamstring muscles are supplied by the:

options.B: Tibial portion of the sciatic nerve (the short head of biceps by the common peroneal)

questions.explanation: Semitendinosus, semimembranosus and long head of biceps: tibial division; short head of biceps: common peroneal division.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The anterior fibres of the deltoid mainly produce:
questions.explanation: Middle fibres abduct; posterior fibres extend and laterally rotate.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which rotator cuff muscle is the main lateral rotator together with teres minor?
questions.explanation: Subscapularis medially rotates; supraspinatus initiates abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which exercise best strengthens the infraspinatus and teres minor?

options.A: Shoulder lateral rotation with elastic tubing

questions.explanation: Lateral rotation (e.g. side-lying with a light dumbbell) isolates these two muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which muscle prevents winging of the scapula?
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the scapula against the thoracic wall.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The biceps brachii is MOST powerful as an elbow flexor when the forearm is:
questions.explanation: In supination the biceps has a better moment arm; brachioradialis is strongest in mid-prone.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which muscle is the strongest flexor of the elbow regardless of forearm position?
questions.explanation: Brachialis attaches to the ulna so is unaffected by forearm rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Pronation of the forearm is performed mainly by:
questions.explanation: Median nerve supply (anterior interosseous for pronator quadratus).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The principal muscle of quiet inspiration is the:
questions.explanation: Contraction flattens the dome, increasing the vertical thoracic dimension. Quiet expiration is passive.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The gait cycle begins with:

options.C: Heel strike (initial contact) of one foot

questions.explanation: The cycle is divided into stance (60%) and swing (40%) phases.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which is NOT a subphase of the stance phase?
questions.explanation: Stance: initial contact, loading response, mid-stance, terminal stance, pre-swing. Swing: initial, mid, terminal swing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Stride length is the distance between:

options.B: Two successive heel strikes of the same foot
options.C: Heel strike of one foot and the other foot

questions.explanation: Stride = two steps; step length = distance between consecutive heel strikes of opposite feet.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The normal walking cadence of an adult is about:
questions.explanation: Cadence = steps per minute; speed ~1.3 m/s.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The total pelvic rotation in the transverse plane during normal walking is about:
questions.explanation: Determinants of gait (Saunders et al.) reduce vertical and lateral displacement of the centre of gravity: pelvic rotation, pelvic tilt, knee flexion in stance, foot/ankle motion, knee motion, lateral displacement of pelvis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A patient with weak quadriceps typically walks with:

options.B: A backward trunk lean or hand pushing on the thigh to keep the knee locked in stance
options.D: Excessive knee flexion at heel strike

questions.explanation: Compensation: extending the knee by moving the centre of gravity in front of the knee axis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: An antalgic gait is characterised by:

options.B: A prolonged stance on the painful limb
options.D: A shortened stance phase on the painful limb

questions.explanation: The patient reduces weight-bearing time on the painful limb.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Excessive hip hiking during swing is a compensation for:

options.C: Inadequate limb clearance (e.g. a stiff knee or foot drop)

questions.explanation: Circumduction and hiking help the foot clear the floor when knee flexion or ankle dorsiflexion is inadequate.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A ‘foot slap’ at initial contact indicates weakness of the:
questions.explanation: Eccentric control of plantar flexion is lost, so the foot drops quickly onto the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: During the loading response of walking, the vertical ground reaction force peaks at about:
questions.explanation: Vertical GRF shows a double hump: first at weight acceptance, a dip at mid-stance (~80%) and second peak at push-off.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Compared with normal gait, a patient using crutches (non-weight bearing) has:
questions.explanation: Crutch walking requires 2–3 times the oxygen consumption of normal gait for amputees and non-weight-bearing patients.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In the stress–strain curve of connective tissue, the ‘toe region’ represents:

options.D: Straightening of crimped collagen fibres with little force

questions.explanation: Elastic region follows; beyond the yield point deformation is plastic; then failure.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Creep in connective tissue refers to:

options.C: Progressive deformation under a constant load over time
options.D: A decrease in force at a constant length

questions.explanation: Low-load prolonged stretching exploits creep; stress relaxation is the decrease in stress when held at constant length.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which statement about collagen is correct?

options.A: Collagen fibres resist tensile forces and give tendons and ligaments strength
options.B: Collagen resists compression better than tension
options.C: Type II collagen is found mainly in tendons
options.D: Collagen is elastic and stretches by 100%

questions.explanation: Type I collagen predominates in tendons, ligaments, bone and skin; type II in hyaline cartilage.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The correct order of soft tissue healing is:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory (days 0–5), repair/proliferation (days 4–21) and remodelling (21 days to 1+ years).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: During the remodelling stage of tendon healing, controlled mechanical stress:

options.B: Aligns collagen fibres along the lines of stress and improves tensile strength

questions.explanation: Wolff's law for bone and Davis's law for soft tissue: tissues remodel along the lines of applied force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Wolff's law states that:

options.A: Bone adapts its structure to the loads placed on it
options.B: Bone growth is independent of load
options.C: Muscle adapts to disuse by hypertrophy

questions.explanation: Increased loading increases bone density; disuse leads to osteopenia.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Articular cartilage receives its nutrition mainly from:

options.B: Synovial fluid by diffusion, assisted by joint movement and compression

questions.explanation: Cartilage is avascular and aneural; cyclic loading pumps fluid in and out.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: A complete tear of a ligament is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Grade I: stretch with minimal fibre damage; grade II: partial tear; grade III: complete rupture with instability. Strain refers to muscle/tendon.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Tendons heal slowly compared with muscle mainly because:

options.B: Of relatively poor vascularity and low metabolic activity
options.D: They contain too many blood vessels

questions.explanation: Hypovascular zones (e.g. supraspinatus critical zone, Achilles) have limited healing capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: After prolonged immobilisation, the strength of ligaments:

options.B: Decreases due to loss of collagen and weak cross-link formation

questions.explanation: Ligament insertion sites weaken fastest; recovery takes much longer than the immobilisation period.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In a muscle immobilised in a shortened position the typical adaptation is:

options.D: Loss of sarcomeres in series, so the muscle becomes shorter

questions.explanation: Muscles adapt to their functional length; immobilised in lengthened position they add sarcomeres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Muscle hypertrophy is mainly due to:

options.B: Increase in the size (cross-sectional area) of existing muscle fibres
options.C: Increase in the number of fibres

questions.explanation: Resistance training increases myofibril number and protein content within fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which cells are responsible for forming new bone during fracture healing?
questions.explanation: Osteoblasts lay down osteoid, osteoclasts resorb bone and remodel callus.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Intradiscal pressure of the lumbar spine is HIGHEST in:

options.A: Sitting while leaning forward with a load

questions.explanation: Nachemson: supine 25%, side-lying 75%, standing 100%, sitting 140%, sitting flexed with load 275%.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In lumbar flexion, the nucleus pulposus moves:
questions.explanation: Flexion compresses the anterior annulus and pushes the nucleus backward; extension moves it forward (McKenzie principle).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Anterior pelvic tilt increases:
questions.explanation: Tight hip flexors and weak abdominals increase anterior pelvic tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The lumbar facet joints are oriented mainly in the:

options.A: Sagittal plane, allowing flexion/extension and limiting rotation

questions.explanation: Cervical facets lie at ~45°, thoracic in the coronal plane (rotation and lateral flexion), lumbar in the sagittal plane.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which cervical joint contributes about 50% of the total cervical rotation?
questions.explanation: Atlanto-occipital joint is mainly flexion/extension (nodding).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which spinal curves are primary (present at birth)?
questions.explanation: Secondary curves (cervical and lumbar lordosis) develop with head control and sitting/walking.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
